correctness.rationale: For all a,b>0 distinct and integers q>=3, the standard integer-redundancy Zak identity yields F_q=sum_j|Zg(x,omega+j/q)|^2. Root-of-unity grouping gives the rational two-tail q-residue formula. Its positive-affine numerator over a strictly decreasing positive denominator is strictly increasing in cos(2pi q omega). At phase +1, a sum of squares of positive exponential sums is strictly convex in x, so the unique endpoint max is B. At phase -1, the derivative reduces to bVt^2+(a-b)Wt-aU with one positive root; equal endpoint values force this root into (1,e^(a+b)). Strict UV>W^2 ensures A>0. The analytic argument establishes all infinite quantifiers; separately implemented truncated-Zak and rational checks passed 6246 supplementary assertions.

value.rationale: The spectral lower and upper constants and their attainment are natural reconstruction-conditioning invariants of a fixed higher-density lattice, beyond qualitative frame existence. An infinite family of q>=3 is solved at arbitrary two positive unequal decay rates, with a unique skew-shifted spatial minimizer and explicit finite-sum plus quadratic-radical formulas. The q>=3 quantitative specialization is not a random numerical slice or a known-table recomputation.
